meta.location: Among the Nephites, at a gathering of the twelve
meta.unit: The name and the gospel (3 Nephi 27)
principles: A dispute settled by a definition
The gospel stated in five verses
Records named as the basis of judgment

world_behind.title: The disciples were on the road when it happened
world_behind.text: Verse 1 has them journeying, preaching, baptizing, and gathered in mighty prayer and fasting. This is not the temple gathering of 3 Nephi 11 through 18 but the working ministry that follows it, and 4 Nephi 1:1 picks up the same labor.

world_behind.title: The naming dispute had precedent
world_behind.text: Mosiah 18:17 has Alma's converts called the church of God, or the church of Christ, and Mosiah 25:23 counts seven churches in the land of Zarahemla. Verse 3 reports the same question reaching the disciples a century and a half later.

world_behind.title: The record has already answered it
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 26:21 says those who were baptized in the name of Jesus were called the church of Christ. The answer stands one chapter before the disputation in verse 3 is reported, which is an artifact of how Mormon has arranged his material.

world_behind.title: The gospel is defined without a citation
world_behind.text: Verses 13 to 15 state it as what he was sent to do and why, and nowhere in the passage is an earlier prophet quoted or a scripture appealed to. 3 Nephi 11:31 to 39 had called the same content his doctrine; sixteen chapters later the same material is given a different label and no supporting text.

world_behind.title: The rule about books is not new here
world_behind.text: Verses 25 and 26 make written records the basis on which people are judged. 2 Nephi 29:11 says the same thing in the Lord's own voice: out of the books which shall be written I will judge the world. This is the reason the record keeps insisting on being written.

world_behind.title: The fourth generation was named a century earlier
world_behind.text: Verse 32 says the fourth generation from this one will be led away captive. Alma 45:12 gave the same span about seventy years before Christ, and Helaman 13:10 repeats it. Three prophecies from three vantage points fix on the same generation.

world_behind.title: This is the last long speech of the ministry
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 28 turns to the disciples' own desires, and 3 Nephi 29 and 30 are Mormon speaking to the reader. The final extended teaching in the book is spent on what to call themselves and what the gospel is.

words.text: Going without food for a religious purpose. The record uses the word seven times and the King James Bible seventeen. Verse 1 pairs it with mighty prayer.
To complain in a low, persistent way. Treated at 1 Nephi 2:11. It appears twenty-five times in the record, and the King James Bible nine.
Clothing, and in the prophets the state of a person before God. The record uses the word thirty-seven times and the King James Bible one hundred and three. Verse 19 has them washed in his blood.
Made holy, set apart. The word turns up ten times here, and the King James Bible sixty-two. Verse 20 attaches it to receiving the Holy Ghost.

Those who decide cases. The record uses the word one hundred and forty times, most of them for the Nephite civil office, and the King James Bible fifty-two. Verse 27 gives the twelve a different kind of bench.
To strike a door for entry. Its count is three times in this book, while the King James Bible four. Verse 29 repeats the promise from the sermon at 3 Nephi 14:7.
Ruin, being utterly lost. The record uses the word twice, here and at 3 Nephi 29:7, and the King James Bible eight times. Verse 32 uses it in a comparison about the fourth generation.

phrases.term: United in mighty prayer and fasting
phrases.text: The condition of the twelve when he appears. Verse 2 gives the praying as the reason.

phrases.term: What will ye that I shall give unto you?
phrases.text: An open offer. What they ask for is a name for the church.

phrases.term: There are disputations among the people concerning this matter
phrases.text: The problem stated plainly. The question is practical and the answer turns out to be doctrinal.

phrases.term: Have they not read the scriptures?
phrases.text: The answer sends them back to a text. He treats the dispute as a reading failure.

phrases.term: If a church be called in Moses' name then it be Moses' church
phrases.text: The rule stated by example. Verse 8 adds the second condition: it must also be built on his gospel.

phrases.term: They have joy in their works for a season
phrases.text: An honest note about what building on the wrong foundation feels like. The failure is described as delayed.

phrases.term: This is the gospel which I have given unto you
phrases.text: The definition announced before it is given. Verses 13 to 15 are the content.

phrases.term: That as I have been lifted up by men even so should men be lifted up by the Father
phrases.text: One verb used two ways. The lifting on the cross and the lifting to judgment are named with the same word.

phrases.term: Those who have washed their garments in my blood
phrases.text: The requirement for entering his rest. Verse 19 lists faith, repentance, and faithfulness to the end alongside it.

phrases.term: What manner of men ought ye to be? Verily I say unto you, even as I am
phrases.text: A question he answers himself. It follows immediately from telling them they will be judges.

phrases.term: It sorroweth me because of the fourth generation from this generation
phrases.text: Grief stated about people not yet born. Verses 30 and 31 had just said none of this generation are lost.

verses.label: v. 1–7
verses.title: A chapter answering an administrative question
verses.text: The disciples' request is practical and the record says why it was asked: "tell us the name whereby we shall call this church; for there are disputations among the people concerning this matter." What follows is the most name-saturated chapter in scripture. Name is used nineteen times here across eleven verses, and no other chapter of the Bible or this volume uses it as often. The answer arrives in verse 7 as three parallel instructions: do it in my name, call the church in my name, call upon the Father in my name.

verses.label: v. 8
verses.title: The argument by substitution
verses.text: The reasoning is put as a test the hearers can run themselves: "if a church be called in Moses' name then it be Moses' church; or if it be called in the name of a man then it be the church of a man." Two substitutions, one with a name the audience reveres and one with a blank. Nothing is asserted about Moses; the sentence works by showing that the rule applies uniformly, and the conclusion about the third case is left for the reader to supply.

verses.label: v. 9–11
verses.title: One preposition, five times
verses.text: Built is used five times in this chapter and every use falls between verses 8 and 11. Each time it governs the same preposition and the alternatives are stated in pairs: "ye are built upon my gospel," "if the church is built upon my gospel then will the Father show forth his own works in it," "if it be not built upon my gospel, and is built upon the works of men, or upon the works of the devil." The whole test of a church is reduced to what it stands on, and the word disappears from the chapter after verse 11.

verses.label: v. 23–26
verses.title: An instruction to write, with an exception
verses.text: The command is specific and it carves out a category: "Write the things which ye have seen and heard, save it be those which are forbidden." Verse 24 extends it forward, to "the works of this people, which shall be," and verses 25 and 26 give the reason: judgment will proceed out of the books. Set beside 3 Ne. 5:18, where the writer says some things cannot be written because of the language, this gives the volume two separate reasons for omission. One is inability and this one is prohibition, and neither is ever lifted.

verses.label: v. 30–32
verses.title: Joy and sorrow, counted by generation
verses.text: The chapter's last statement about the future is arithmetic. Of the people in front of him, "none of them are lost." Of what comes after, "it sorroweth me because of the fourth generation from this generation." The volume has made this count twice before. 2 Ne. 26:9 gives the same interval, peace "until three generations shall have passed away, and many of the fourth generation shall have passed away in righteousness," and Alma 45:10 sets the term at four hundred years. Three passages, written centuries apart in the story, arrive at the same boundary.

chapter.title: A practical dispute gets a doctrinal answer
chapter.text: Verse 3 asks what to call the church and verses 5 through 9 answer with what a name means. The small question opens a large one.

chapter.title: He points them to reading
chapter.text: Verse 5 asks whether they have read the scriptures. The remedy for the dispute is already written down.

chapter.title: The name has a second condition
chapter.text: Verse 8 requires the gospel underneath the label. The name alone does not settle it.

chapter.title: The gospel is stated in five verses
chapter.text: Verses 13 through 18 give it start to finish. It is short enough to memorize and is framed as a definition.

chapter.title: Wrong foundations feel fine for a while
chapter.text: Verse 11 grants the builders a season of gladness. The chapter does not pretend the error is obvious early.

chapter.title: Judgment is tied to writing
chapter.text: Verses 25 and 26 make the books the basis. What gets recorded matters to the outcome.

chapter.title: The standard for the twelve is himself
chapter.text: Verse 27 answers its own question with two words. Nothing lower is offered.

chapter.title: Joy and grief sit next to each other
chapter.text: Verses 30 and 31 say none of this generation are lost and verse 32 grieves over the fourth. The chapter holds both in three sentences.

applications.title: Ask the question you actually have
applications.text: They asked what to call the church, naming the reason plainly, "there are disputations among the people concerning this matter." What came back was a definition of what a church is. Small administrative questions are worth bringing; they often turn out to be the doorway to the larger one.

applications.title: Check whether it is already written
applications.text: He answered a dispute by asking whether they had read. Some arguments end when someone opens the book, and the fastest way to find out is to look before arguing further.

applications.title: Test the foundation, not the label
applications.text: A name in his name is his church only if it is built on his gospel, and verse 11 gives the failing case in the same terms, a work built "upon the works of men, or upon the works of the devil." Apply the test to something you belong to: not what it is called, but what it is standing on.

applications.title: Say what the word means before you use it
applications.text: The chapter stops to define its central term outright, "this is the gospel which I have given unto you," which the volume rarely does. When a discussion keeps circling, the useful move is to state your definition and let people disagree with that.

applications.title: Notice a phrase facing two ways
applications.text: "Lifted up" means the cross in verse 14 and the reward in verse 22, eight verses apart and with no comment. Words you use about your own life carry more than one direction; check which one you have been hearing.

applications.title: Write it down for the use it will be put to
applications.text: The command carves out an exception, "save it be those which are forbidden," and then gives the purpose, that judgment proceeds out of the books. Records made for a known future use get kept differently from notes made for yourself.

applications.title: Say the same thing at the end that you said at the beginning
applications.text: The last two sentences of the visit are the two he opened his teaching with, thirteen chapters earlier at 3 Nephi 14:7 and 14:13. When you have said something that mattered, the closing is a place to repeat it rather than to add.

applications.title: Count the good news and the bad news the same way
applications.text: Of the people present, "none of them are lost." Of the fourth generation, sorrow. Both are stated as arithmetic and neither is softened by the other. Report on what you care about with the same precision in both directions.

questions.text: When did I last fast with other people over one question?
What dispute of mine would end if I read more carefully?
Is what I am building on his gospel or on my own work?
What have I had joy in for a season that is not going to hold?
What in me is still unclean?
What manner of man ought I to be today?
Which gate am I actually walking through?
